paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The rulers in Jerusalem picked a hiding place that was built on lies, and a lie can't hold weight when the flood comes. They said they had a covenant with death, and the Lord GOD told them that covenant "will be dissolved" (Isaiah 28:18). Whatever you trust besides God, it's a cardboard umbrella in a hurricane, baker, and I have stood under a few of those myself.

So where do you go instead? Right in the middle of the warning, the Lord GOD says, "See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; the one who believes will never be shaken" (Isaiah 28:16). Peter, an apostle of Jesus, applies that stone to Jesus (1 Peter 2:4-6). Your safety was never in a clever deal or a good hiding place. It's in Him, and He's already been laid.

Then Isaiah turns to a farmer, and the farmer teaches us one more thing. He plows, plants and threshes each seed the right way, because "his God instructs and teaches him properly" (Isaiah 28:26). The LORD of Hosts is "wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom" (Isaiah 28:29), so His hand is never random. So stop scoffing, baker, build on the stone, and trust the One whose wisdom is wonderful.
